summary: The COVID-19 pandemic continues to have a significant impact on our city, with variants of concern requiring continued public health measures to decrease the risk of transmission and the risk of serious illness or death. While COVID-19 cases and hospitalization rates are trending downward, it is imperative that all people in Toronto adhere to the recommended public health measures and draw on lessons learned in waves 1, 2, and 3 of the COVID-19 pandemic. The City's vaccination campaign throughout the month of May has continued to be a critical strategy to mitigate the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, the expansion of pop-up and mobile vaccine clinics has been especially successful in facilitating vaccine delivery and ensuring those at greatest risk have access to vaccines. This report provides an update on the Toronto Public Health response to the COVID-19 pandemic, in partnership with City divisions, health system partners, and community stakeholders. In addition, this report includes an update on COVID-19 equity indicators, as requested by the Board of Health in October 2020, and an overview of the status and trends in workplace COVID-19 outbreaks, as directed by the Board of Health in January 2021.
